SPY：756-760是多头最后一道重要防线
SPY 已经跌破前几天横盘整理时的一些短期均线和弱支撑，现在正在靠近 756-760这个核心区域。这里有前期结构支撑，同时也是多头是否还能维持当前节奏的关键位置。

如果 SPY 能在 756-760 一带企稳，并且后面出现比较明确的反包、长下影或者放量止跌，那就是还是正常回踩，后面重新挑战前高的逻辑还是成立。

It's very common for us to become max bearish at the worst possible time. 

And here timeframes matter, intermediate term I am a little worried, because longer term breadth has a long way to go to become oversold, and we see clear cracks with lack of followthrough and a choppy environment.

But short term this is not the spot to become overly bearish, we are the most oversold we have been since the March low.

Oversold is not a buy signal, we can always become more oversold, and the highest volatility and fastest declines occur from oversold conditions. 

But this is an important piece of the puzzle to understand in the underlying market, if weakness is temporary this is where we usually soon snapback.

But zooming out this is my favorite chart, the monthly chart of the S&P 500. And here is a trick you should pay attention to.

Whenever we come close to the monthly EMA 50 I load up the truck in my children's account and my own longer term portfolio. We don't get many shots at that in our lifetime, when others see danger - see opportunity. 

The other observation is, this channel has been respected for 17 years, and it will likely be respected again.

Consistency in trading became a whole lot easier when my mornings became boringly predictable.

If you know me already, you know I'm a man of simplicity. So when something works, I stick with it.

Here is my EXACT morning routine I’ve repeated for years before the market opens:

Preface: my trading day doesn't actually start when the market opens, because by the time the opening bell rings, most of the important decisions have already been made.

Like my system, my morning routine has barely changed over the last few years. I don't wake up looking for something new to trade. I'm simply preparing for the plans I made the night before. My watchlist is already built, I know the pivots I'm interested in, and I already have an idea of what would make me buy, sell, or do absolutely nothing.

Every morning starts about 1 hour before the open (7:30 AM CST).

The first thing I do is open my Bible.

My faith is of utmost importance, so that's non-negotiable. It reminds me that my identity isn't tied to whether today is green/red or my P&L on any given day. Trading is important to me, but it's not the most important thing in my life. Starting my day with Jesus makes it a whole lot easier to keep the market in its proper place.

Then I get some coffee going (also non-negotiable) and start getting caught up on what's happened overnight.

I'll look through earnings if need be, check for any news that could impact names I'm watching or currently own, see where futures are trading, and get a feel for how the market is likely to open. The entire goal is simply trying to eliminate surprises.

From there, I review every open position I currently have, and within this market recently it's been extremely light. I update my stops if needed, adjust my trading plan, and set alerts around important levels of interest. I want my phone & charts doing the work for me instead of staring at every tick all day.

It's a common fact now that emotion usually shows up when preparation is missing. If I'm making every decision in real time while candles are flying around, I'm far more likely to chase, hesitate, or second-guess myself, and/or force something that isn't there.

That's why I try to solve as many problems as possible before the market even opens.

By the time 8:30 CST rolls around, I don't want to be asking, "What should I do?" I want to be asking, "Is the market confirming my plan?"

I think a lot of people assume consistency comes from other concepts like finding a better setup, entry tactic, or a new indicator. And yes, those matter... but in my experience, it comes from doing the same boring things every single morning until they become second nature.

The market changes every single day, but my consistent routine doesn't.

And I think that's a huge reason I can stay objective when everyone else seems to be reacting emotionally... especially in this current environment!

I hope this helps, God bless.

The messier the market gets, the more important your process becomes.

When conditions are clean, almost everything works. Breakouts follow through, leaders stay strong, breadth expands, and even average setups can make you look smarter than you are.

The problem is that those periods can hide a weak process.

When the market gets choppy, rotational, narrow, or full of false starts, that’s when random stock picking starts getting exposed.

This is why I like working top-down.

Start with the market.

Before looking at individual stocks, I want to know what kind of environment I’m dealing with.

Is trend healthy?
Is breadth expanding or contracting?
Are internals risk-on or deteriorating?
Is distribution building?
A good setup in a bad environment is a very different trade than the same setup in a healthy one.

Then look at rotation.

What is gaining strength vs what?

Growth vs Value.
Semis vs the market.
Small caps vs large caps.
Equal weight vs cap weight.
Discretionary vs staples.
This helps answer a simple question:
Where is the market actually rewarding exposure? https://t.co/luJo5fMvRb

Then move into themes and groups.

Instead of finding a random stock and building a story around it, I’d rather start where strength is already concentrated.

Which themes are leading?
Which groups are improving?
Where is momentum persistent across timeframes?
That narrows the universe fast.

Then find the leaders.

Not every stock going up is a leader.

I want the names with real relative strength, liquidity, persistence, proper structure, and ideally a strong group behind them.

That’s where the highest-quality opportunities usually live. https://t.co/0OFhC7EyQi

Setups come last.

Only after all of that do I really care about the entry.

Reclaims.
Pullbacks.
Tightening.
Breakouts.

Backtests.
The setup matters, but the context around the setup matters just as much.

That’s basically the workflow we built TradersLab around:
Market → Internals → Rotation → Themes → Leaders → Setups

The goal isn’t to predict everything.

It’s to reduce noise until you’re spending your time where the odds are actually better.

That becomes even more important when the market stops being easy.

The Yen Carry Trade Unwinding (2026)
BoJ's response to Bessent's "I am the House Now"

It appears that there is no conclusion to human's greed, that Japanese YEN carry trade continue to explode to a record high in 2026. 

(March 2026 Jefferies/BIS proxy of ~$2.35 trillion in cross-border yen borrowing, or Morgan Stanley's more conservative estimate of $500 billion in mid-2026).

Despite Bessent's threat, BoJ unloads their US Treasuries onto the market (to get the USD to support Yen, concurrently if you notice the USD recently not rising in line with yield ==> a non-domestic player is dumping), that possibly explains some of the yield spike we saw (of course there are other reasons e.g. inflation expectation/ rate hike expectation/ higher uncertainty). Bear in mind being no expert, a lot of this is just personal guessworks, you may supplement with facts and corrections if any.

Everything has a cost.

The huge Yen Carry Trade is unwinding ahead of Yen appreciation (more costly when converted back into Yen to repay) and also higher cost of borrowing (in anticipation of at least 0.25% hike by BoJ this September).

1. How does this affect your US stocks?

When Yen Carry Trade is unwinding, they will be selling your US assets (bonds, stocks). This is mechanical ~ nothing to do with your technical analysis, or a company's fundamentals. I learned this lesson the hardway in summer 2024.

2. How long will the selling last?

I don't know, this thing is much bigger than, and the market should be more efficient than me.
i) Maybe just starting, many more to come
ii) Maybe already in progress, but more to come
iii) Maybe already towards the end, if the YEN speculators can stop their greed and if both Japan and US are happy at the current levels.

3. What Should You Do?

Just need to be aware, but don't let this noise influence you.

Stick to YOUR process and your timeframe, and just trade (or sit out) what you see. 

Risk management is non-negotiable.

There is no winners or losers in this game, only survivor.
